clue.text: Army commander in the county needs underground rest rooms

indicators.note: the military pair sits inside the county name, which wraps around them

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
Commanding Officer
short for Cambridgeshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A general stationed in the shire has to find toilets below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest rooms' suggests toilets, but here the rest is eternal. CAMBS is the standard abbreviation for Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are subterranean burial galleries, where the dead lie at rest, so they are literally chambers for resting below ground.

clue.text: Sculpt, with head of Venus in mind

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken from the goddess's name
in places one letter inside the word for mind

blocks.note: to mind is to care
its first letter

explanation.surface: An artist sculpts with a statue of Venus in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to shape stone or wood by cutting, which is what sculpting is.

clue.text: Ancient Greek uses the imperfect

indicators.note: imperfect means flawed, so the words are not in their proper form and are rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: the classical author writes in the imperfect tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imperfect' looks like the grammatical tense, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the legendary Athenian hero who slew the Minotaur, a Greek figure from antiquity.

clue.text: Froggy's pursuit, we hear, didn't miss the boat

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: not missing the boat means catching the vessel

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's chase in which he just managed to board his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Froggy is the frog in the nursery song 'A frog he would a-wooing go'. In British speech court and caught sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing is what the frog of the nursery rhyme sets out to do, and wooing means paying romantic attention.

clue.text: Force a cretin when flustered to check

indicators.note: someone flustered is agitated and confused, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to make someone do something is to force them
the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Pressure a fool, while he is rattled, into keeping someone in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to verify it, ensuring beyond doubt that it is so.

clue.text: Bribe for Sabbath work

blocks.note: S is short for Sunday, the Christian Sabbath
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is paid off to work on the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small concession or payment given to placate or buy off someone.

clue.text: Semi-serious part for a tightwad

indicators.note: only a portion of the hyphenated phrase is wanted, a run of consecutive letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen, from the end of the first part into the second

explanation.surface: An actor is cast in a half-comic role playing a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who hoards money and hates spending it; tightwad is an informal synonym.

clue.text: Put up, say. Lily Langtry'S first picture

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top
first takes only the opening letter of the actress's surname

blocks.note: an arum is one kind of lily, which 'say' signals
the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Lillie Langtry, the Victorian actress, has her portrait hung for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily Langtry' reads as a name, but Lily is the flower and Langtry gives one letter; 'say' marks the arum as an example of a lily.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural is a painting applied directly to a wall, so it is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Person whose English is initially slipshod

blocks.note: a sloven is a careless, slipshod person
E is the abbreviation for English
places the careless word at the start, before the single letter

explanation.surface: A foreigner whose grasp of English starts out sloppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is initially slipshod' says the careless word comes before the letter for English.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene is a native of Slovenia, so the answer is indeed a person, defined very loosely.

clue.text: Harassed person turns red — he has to give the reply

definitions.text: he has to give the reply

indicators.note: a harassed person is flustered and disordered, so those letters are mixed up
turns means the colour word is flipped to run backwards

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
taken as written before it is flipped

explanation.surface: A flustered man blushes because he must answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A responder is one who answers, so he is the person obliged to give the reply.

clue.text: Eggs a dollar? Sounds dear

blocks.note: roe is fish eggs
buck is slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A shopper complains that eggs at a dollar seem expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds dear' reads as 'seems expensive', fitting the price talk, but it is the definition: a word that sounds like dear, namely deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is the male of the roe species, a small Eurasian deer, matching the animal the spoken word names.

clue.text: Mean parasite almost desperate

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the creature's name is dropped

blocks.note: par is the average or norm
a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A nasty, desperate bloodsucker of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for the parasite, but it is a noun: the average, par.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous means perilous or dire, describing a situation so bad that it borders on hopeless.

clue.text: Throw out what is unsatisfactory right away

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is sent away, removed from the word for unsatisfactory

blocks.note: a reject is a substandard item
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Bin anything that is not up to scratch immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'immediately', but it splits: R, then the instruction to take it away.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to expel or force out, the same as throwing someone or something out.

clue.text: Political clique with possible role for a Spaniard

indicators.note: possible suggests one of several ways the word could be arranged, not the one written

blocks.note: a cabal is a secret political faction
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A secretive political faction has a part lined up for a man from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish word for a gentleman or horseman, so it names a Spanish man.

clue.text: Key-ring given with purchase at this sale

blocks.note: B is a musical key
taken as written
and joins one thing with another
a buy is a purchase

explanation.surface: A key ring thrown in free with something bought at a jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key-ring' looks like one object, but the hyphen hides two parts. A bring-and-buy is a British charity sale where people donate goods and buy others'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a charity sale where people bring items to sell and buy what others have brought.

clue.text: Step here round trench

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a sap is a military trench dug towards the enemy

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to step over here, around the trench.
explanation.walkthrough: A sap is an old military term for a covered trench used in sieges.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas is a ballet term borrowed from French for a single dance step or movement.

clue.text: Delayed, so stopped on indefinitely

indicators.note: indefinitely means in no fixed way, so the letters are not kept in their set order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A project held up, halted for an unlimited time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indefinitely' fits the idea of delay so well that it hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something postponed has been put off until a later time, which is exactly being delayed.

clue.text: It should suit one of the watermen

definitions.text: It should suit one of the watermen

blocks.note: surface: something that will please or fit a person; setter's reading: a cloth that is made into suits
surface: a boatman or ferryman; setter's reading: a fabric named after an island and a river, so sounding like a man whose name is all water

explanation.surface: Something that ought to please a Thames boatman.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a tweed cloth from the Hebridean island of Harris; the name sounds like a person, and both halves are watery, an island and a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: This handwoven woollen fabric from the Outer Hebrides is classically tailored into jackets and suits.

clue.text: To kill white ant, feed with sodium

indicators.note: feeding puts something inside, so the insect takes the chemical symbol into itself

blocks.note: termites are often called white ants
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Instructions for poisoning termites with sodium.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminate is a euphemism for killing, ending someone's life, as in assassin's or thriller slang.

clue.text: Traveller held up in the tube

definitions.text: Traveller held up in the tube

blocks.note: surface: a passenger delayed or robbed; setter's reading: someone literally supported, holding on overhead
surface: just where the delay happened; setter's reading: on the London Underground, called the Tube, standing in a crowded carriage

explanation.surface: A passenger is delayed on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' means delayed in the surface, but literally means supported: standing commuters on the Tube grip hanging straps.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing commuter on a crowded train or bus who grips an overhead loop for balance is called this.

clue.text: Underdone portion of savoury

blocks.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
a bit is a portion

explanation.surface: A complaint that a helping of a savoury dish is undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A savoury, in British usage, is a small salty dish served at the end of a meal; Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, toasted cheese, is a classic British savoury course.

clue.text: Spoil from mother earth's core

indicators.note: the core of something is its centre, so only the central letter of the planet's name is kept

blocks.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
the middle of five letters

explanation.surface: Damage done from the very heart of Mother Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother earth' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to damage or disfigure, much as to spoil something ruins its quality.

clue.text: Wild horse cannot but upset nag

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disarranged, so the old horse's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: if you cannot but do something, you must
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An untamed stallion is bound to unsettle an old nag.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a free-roaming horse of the American West, descended from Spanish stock.

clue.text: Some woman attached to the Temple

blocks.note: some means a part of
hen is informal for a woman
on means attached or joined to

explanation.surface: A certain woman is devoted to the Temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some woman' reads as a single phrase, but it breaks into separate words. The Temple might suggest the London law district.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the famous ancient temple of Athena on the Athens Acropolis, the temple above all others.

clue.text: Having heaps of folk music without charge

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for charge is removed from the music style

blocks.note: hillbilly is rural American folk music
a bill is a charge

explanation.surface: A free concert with lots of folk music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without charge' suggests free of cost, but charge is a word to take out.
explanation.definitionFit: Land described this way has many hills, humorously called heaps or mounds.

clue.text: Trendy group put inside

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A fashionable crowd gets locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To inset something is to fix or insert it within another thing, as a panel into a frame.

clue.text: One perhaps may be tickled to death

definitions.text: One perhaps may be tickled to death

blocks.note: surface: an idiom for delighted; setter's reading: literally caught by tickling and then killed
surface: some person might be thrilled; setter's reading: a fish that poachers catch by stroking its belly

explanation.surface: Someone might well be thoroughly delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickling is a poacher's way of catching this fish by hand: stroking its underside until it can be flipped out.
explanation.definitionFit: This river fish is famously caught by hand-tickling, after which it is killed for the table.

clue.text: Blue ran off like a cloud of dust

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or not right, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A blue colour bled out, leaving a dusty smudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is an interstellar cloud of gas and dust, so nebular describes something of that hazy kind.

clue.text: Climbing tree from N Africa

definitions.note: the answer is a name, the Rif region of Morocco, used as an adjective

indicators.note: climbing goes upwards, so in a down clue the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A climbing tree native to North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rif is a mountainous region of northern Morocco, whose Berber people are also called Rif.

clue.text: Well done female act — what self-confidence!

blocks.note: brava is the cry of praise to a female performer
to do is to act

explanation.surface: An audience cheers a woman's daring stage turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bravo is shouted for a man, brava for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold show of confidence, often more swagger than substance, which the exclamation captures.

clue.text: Sort of box sailors get for a song

blocks.note: first meaning: a small box where a sailor keeps personal odds and ends
second meaning: a short simple tune

explanation.surface: Sailors are given a kind of box in return for singing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a seaman's small kit box and a short, light piece of music.

clue.text: Astute old person keeps English boxer

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the old person's word wraps around the letter

blocks.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
wight is an archaic word for a person
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A shrewd old man still owns an English boxer dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests the dog breed, but it is a fighter. Fly in British slang means streetwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in the lightest of the standard weight classes.
